I've implemented a fix for the libnvidia-ml.so.1 missing library error in the fix/nvidia-library-mapping branch. This version adds dynamic discovery and bind-mounting of host NVIDIA driver libraries into the LXC container. It also adds a host-side check to verify that drivers are correctly installed on the Proxmox host before starting the configuration.

You can test it by running: `bash <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saihgupr/frigate-proxmox-script/fix/nvidia-library-mapping/install.sh)`
Thanks! I'll test this over the next few days when I get a moment to do so!
The script completes successfully now, but frigate doesn't seem to come up. I'll report back later when I have more time to debug!

I have the same issue with the [install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saihgupr/frigate-proxmox-script/main/install.sh) error at the end, & the same issue in that the[ 'fix'](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saihgupr/frigate-proxmox-script/fix/nvidia-library-mapping/install.sh) script installs successfully. But, although the LXC starts up, Frigate doesn't. Proxmox 9.1.7 HP Proliant ML110 G6, 16gb, Xeon X3450 Nvidia GTX 745 GPU (NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-580.126.09.run installed on Proxmox) Latest Frigate per the script. I may be wrong, but it doesn't look like it's downloading/installing Docker or Frigate in the fix script? EDIT I've run the script twice now. On both attempts I couldn't access the Console or SSH even though I selected to enable SSH and provided a Root password? So I'm unable to access the LXC to see if Docker or Frigate are installed 🤷‍♂️

Found the problem with the nvidia libs. It was only mapping the symlinks and not the actual library files into the container. I fixed it to resolve the links properly now. Give the fix/nvidia-lib-missing-issue30 branch a shot and see if it starts up.

Hey, thanks for the detailed logs. I found a couple of bugs here. First, there was a flaw in the hardware detection that caused the script to exit early if it didn't find a Google Coral.

More importantly, for the NVIDIA error, I've updated the library mapping to be much more thorough. It now scans multiple system paths on the host and automatically updates the container's library cache (ldconfig) on startup.

Give it a shot with the latest branch:
`bash <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saihgupr/frigate-proxmox-script/fix/storage-pool-detection-issue26-34/install.sh)`

Let me know if that clears up the 'libnvidia-ml.so.1' error!

I've pushed a fix to the `fix/nvidia-lib-missing-issue30` branch.

It adds the missing `libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so.1` and `libnvidia-rtcore.so.1` libraries and switches to dynamic detection for the device major numbers. This should fix the `libcuda` error and make the passthrough more reliable across different hosts.

Let me know if that works!
